title: The bottom Grothendieck interval transported to an augmented comparison
statement: Let A,B be Grothendieck abelian categories and C an abelian category, with bounded below derived categories. Let F:A\to B and G:B\to C be additive functors, with F left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Let I resolve X and J resolve F(X) [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let \phi:J\to F(I) satisfy \iota_J^0\phi^0=F(\iota_I^0). Write L for the zero extension of F(I), f for the zero extension of \phi, a_J for resolutionAugmentationIso J, and e_F for canonicalResolutionDerivedIso F I [def-pc-canonical-resolution-derived-iso]. For n\ge0, the inverse bottom-source identification followed by the raw bottom edge [lem-sp-grothendieck-edge-maps] and H^n(RG(e_F)) equals \theta_G^{-1}H^n(RG(a_J))H^n(RG(Qf)), where \theta_G identifies H^n(RG(F(X)[0])) with R^nG(F(X)) [lem-sp-derived-well-defined]. This assertion has no acyclicity hypothesis, no derived-composite comparison, and no identification with homology of G applied to a resolution.

proof.text: Extend J and F(I) by zero. The comparison after the J augmentation is the F(I) augmentation: hphi is exactly the degree-zero equality and all other source terms vanish. Invert the quasi-isomorphism which is the augmentation of J in the derived category. The represented morphism is the canonical map F(X)[0] to RF(X), followed by canonicalResolutionDerivedIso F I.

Left exactness identifies F(X) with H^0(RF(X)), and RF(X) has no negative homology. Under the q=0 truncation isomorphism used in grothendieckBottomEdgeSourceIso, the preceding morphism is the inclusion of the bottom interval into the full interval. Expand q=0, cancel zero shifts, apply RG and H^n, and use preservation of composition. The only remaining source comparison is the inverse single-object homology comparison for G. This proves the displayed Lean equality, before any composite or G-resolution identification.
